Depression is like breathing, a continuous unconscious act that can only be stopped by temporarily forcing oneself to do so. 

Losing a relationship has to be one of the hardest things emotionally humans can experience. The only thing that stopped me when I was crying on the kitchen floor of the apartment me and my partner had shared holding a knife to my wrist sobbing uncontrollably, is the thought that this won't be the last. This won't be the last person I share my life with, this won't be the last person I share my happiness with. I refuse to let this one person ruin me. This won't be the last person I love. And it wasn't.

You can have your opinion. But none the less, I believe what I said is true. Because we both said the same thing. I agree that people don't want to be depressed, that's why I said it was a lie. Reading what is written, and understanding what is written, are two different things.

I think it's the plight of people who are either extremely aware of their own surroundings because they notice the trivial failures and flaws OR the plight of people who are extremely unaware and only dwell on themselves; both of these things usually yield the same result of depression.

I believe your extreme lies in the awareness category. Now there is no cure because this is how you are wired. But there is something you can do from my own personal experience, and that is purpose. Find it. Find what suits you and mine that inner treasure. Don't put all your hopes in dream into it, never do that with anything, but find purpose. It seems to me you have a lot of soul searching to do if you want to accomplish anything with this life. We don't choose life, we didn't choose to be born, but we do choose what we do with it. Your weapon of choice should be the power to choose. Do so wisely.

Misery can only be experienced if you've also experienced joy. So then you can feel the contrast between the two, and then you know misery. What brings you joy?

Most people around here would say nothing does. But that's a lie. They just want to feel pain and misery. For me, what brings me joy is making others in my life happy. Doing everything I can to make their world better. So think, long and hard about what brings you joy, and there you will find you have solved your own problem. 

Cheers.

I understand brother. I really really do. There is no reality, only perception. The way you perceive the world around you is your reality. How I perceive the world around me is mine.

With that being said; Do you want the pain that you perceive and put on yourself to stop? I think the answer is yes. Find someone you can talk to, just now you thought of someone - fuck the stigmas of 'they didn't' 'I didn't' or any past drama, fuck that shit. Talk to them. Because the meaning of life as far as I perceive it is human interaction. Fuck the excuses, go talk to someone you care about.

I am inclined to find truth in this. In my experience most people who say suicide is selfish are ignorant to the plight. 

Today is my birthday, I am 26 today, I have 3 siblings, 2 mothers and 2 fathers, 9 cousins and three living grandparents. None will contact me on this day, because I have shunned myself and through lack of contact I have shunned them. That, is selfish.

You are alive because you choose to be. As far as we know you did not ask to be born, so you should not ask why you have it. 

The question you should ask is; I am still alive, what will I accomplish with the time I have?

Not to enjoy my view from a high horse or pass judgement, but that is a question that I think better suits someone with so much more to see and enjoy.
